text:
maya: heads-up — saw a microburst pattern hitting continuous-batcher yesterday causing an eviction storm. coalesce window was 5ms, many tiny requests clustered and kv-cache misalignment amplified headroom starvation. want to discuss smoothing + interface boundaries :thinking_face:

alex: ugh, that matches the p95 spikes i saw. a couple quick ideas: add leaky-bucket admission smoothing or jitter the coalesce window per-tenant. simple and backward-compatible.

sam: +1 for jittered windows. tradeoff: jitter increases avg latency a bit. also need to think about prefetch alignment — if kv cache prefetches for a batch but the batch gets evicted because of a microburst, we waste work.

kevin: important point about boundaries: runtime scheduler shouldn't own KV layout. i'd rather expose a small signal from the cache (eg. cache_pressure or lease_tokens) than couple scheduler to kv internals. keeps interfaces clean.

li: we prototyped a lease token handshake a while ago — basically: scheduler claims N tokens for an in-flight batch, cache pins corresponding KV pages, returns a token id. if evicted, cache returns a revoke reason. sketch: ```proto
message LeaseRequest { string tenant = 1; int32 tokens = 2; }
message LeaseResponse { bool granted = 1; string token_id = 2; enum Reason { NONE=0; EVICT=1; OOM=2; } reason = 3; }
```

ops-bot: alert: evict-spike service=continuous-batcher region=us-west1 p99_evictions=18/min time=2023-11-05T15:12:03Z

maya: ok — two axes here: short-term smoothing (admission jitter/leaky-bucket, backpressure hints) vs long-term interface (lease tokens / cache_pressure metric). propose we run a short experiment with jittered admission + a lightweight cache_pressure metric first.

alex: volunteer to run experiment. plan: 1) add tenant-level jitter knob (default 5ms +/- 3ms), 2) surface cache_pressure as a numeric gauge (0-1) in batcher telemetry, 3) run A/B on a small set of tenants for 24h.

sam: need to add dashboards to measure impact: queries I'll use — 
- evictions / minutely
- p99 response latency
- tokenized cost per request
I'll draft PromQLs and share.

kevin: for the refactor path: incremental is best. step 0: metrics (cache_pressure). step 1: admission knobs + experiments. step 2: lease-token API if experiments show benefit. also flag: watch for fairness regressions when jittering.

li: default threshold idea: grant lease tokens up to 90% of cache capacity per-tenant, revoke when pressure>0.8. but that's for later — we'll keep it opt-in behind feature flag.

maya: sounds good. action items:
- @alex: implement jitter knob + telemetry (PR by EOD Friday)
- @sam: dashboards and PromQL (PR by Monday)
- @kevin: review metric surface and fairness test plan
- @li: keep lease-token proto draft in a branch for RFC if experiment looks promising

maya: let's sync in 48h to check experiment signals. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
